# Session File Format

Sessions are stored as JSONL (JSON Lines) files. Each line is a JSON object with a `type` field. Session entries form a tree structure via `id`/`parentId` fields, enabling in-place branching without creating new files.

For programmatic creation, persistence, and tree navigation, see the [`SessionManager` API](sdk.md#sessionmanager-api).


## File Location

```
~/.pi/agent/sessions/--<path>--/<timestamp>_<session-id>.jsonl
```

By default, `<session-id>` is a UUID. Callers can supply a custom ID through the SDK or `--session-id`. For `<path>`, Pi removes the leading path separator and replaces `/`, `\\`, and `:` with `-`.

## Deleting Sessions

Sessions can be removed by deleting their `.jsonl` files under `~/.pi/agent/sessions/`.

Pi also supports deleting sessions interactively from `/resume` (select a session and press `Ctrl+D`, then confirm). When available, pi uses the `trash` CLI to avoid permanent deletion.

## Session Version

Sessions have a version field in the header:

- **Version 1**: Linear entry sequence (legacy, auto-migrated on load)
- **Version 2**: Tree structure with `id`/`parentId` linking
- **Version 3**: Renamed `hookMessage` role to `custom` (extensions unification)

Existing sessions are automatically migrated to the current version (v3) when loaded.

## Source Files

Source on GitHub ([pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi)):
- [`packages/coding-agent/src/core/session-manager.ts`](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/packages/coding-agent/src/core/session-manager.ts) - Session entry types and SessionManager
- [Message Types](message-types.md) - Shared message and content-block reference
- [`packages/coding-agent/src/core/messages.ts`](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/packages/coding-agent/src/core/messages.ts) - Extended message types
- [`packages/ai/src/types.ts`](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/packages/ai/src/types.ts) - Base message and content-block types
- [`packages/agent/src/types.ts`](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/packages/agent/src/types.ts) - Extensible `AgentMessage` union

For TypeScript definitions in your project, inspect `node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/` and `node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-ai/dist/`.

## Messages

A `message` entry stores an [`AgentMessage`](message-types.md). Message content blocks, roles, usage, and message timestamps are defined in [Message Types](message-types.md).

Session entry timestamps are ISO 8601 strings. The nested message timestamp is a Unix timestamp in milliseconds.

## Entry Base

All entries (except `SessionHeader`) extend `SessionEntryBase`:

```typescript
interface SessionEntryBase {
  type: string;
  id: string;           // Usually an 8-char hex ID; may fall back to a full UUID
  parentId: string | null;  // Parent entry ID (null for a root entry)
  timestamp: string;    // ISO timestamp
}
```

## Entry Types

### SessionHeader

First line of the file. Metadata only, not part of the tree (no `id`/`parentId`).

```json
{"type":"session","version":3,"id":"uuid","timestamp":"2024-12-03T14:00:00.000Z","cwd":"/path/to/project"}
```

For sessions with a parent (created via `/fork`, `/clone`, or `newSession({ parentSession })`):

```json
{"type":"session","version":3,"id":"uuid","timestamp":"2024-12-03T14:00:00.000Z","cwd":"/path/to/project","parentSession":"/path/to/original/session.jsonl"}
```

### SessionMessageEntry

A message in the conversation. The `message` field contains an `AgentMessage`. System messages carry the prompt and tool loadout: the first request of a session persists one with every prompt section and tool declaration, and later changes persist as system messages that patch `sections` by name (`null` removes one) and list `toolsAdded`/`toolsRemoved`. Replaying them in order yields the current prompt and tools; there is no separate prompt state entry.

```json
{"type":"message","id":"a0b1c2d3","parentId":null,"timestamp":"2024-12-03T14:00:00.000Z","message":{"role":"system","content":"","sections":{"preamble":"You are an expert coding assistant...","tools":"<tools>\n- read: ...\n</tools>","cwd":"/project"},"toolsAdded":[{"name":"read","description":"...","parameters":{}}],"timestamp":1733234400000}}
{"type":"message","id":"d4e5f6g7","parentId":"c3d4e5f6","timestamp":"2024-12-03T14:04:00.000Z","message":{"role":"system","content":"","sections":{"skills":"<skills>...</skills>"},"toolsRemoved":[{"name":"write"}],"timestamp":1733234640000}}
```

Sessions created before system messages existed have no leading system message; the first request declares the current prompt as a later system message, which replays the same way.

```json
{"type":"message","id":"a1b2c3d4","parentId":"prev1234","timestamp":"2024-12-03T14:00:01.000Z","message":{"role":"user","content":"Hello","timestamp":1733234401000}}
{"type":"message","id":"b2c3d4e5","parentId":"a1b2c3d4","timestamp":"2024-12-03T14:00:02.000Z","message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Hi!"}],"api":"anthropic-messages","provider":"anthropic","model":"claude-sonnet-4-5","usage":{...},"stopReason":"stop","timestamp":1733234402000}}
{"type":"message","id":"c3d4e5f6","parentId":"b2c3d4e5","timestamp":"2024-12-03T14:00:03.000Z","message":{"role":"toolResult","toolCallId":"call_123","toolName":"bash","content":[{"type":"text","text":"output"}],"isError":false,"timestamp":1733234403000}}
```

Assistant messages name the model that produced them. Newer messages also record `thinkingLevel`, the Pi thinking level requested for that response.

### ModelChangeEntry

Emitted when the user switches models mid-session. The latest entry is the selected model, which may be a [virtual model](virtual-models.md); assistant messages then name the physical model that answered.

```json
{"type":"model_change","id":"d4e5f6g7","parentId":"c3d4e5f6","timestamp":"2024-12-03T14:05:00.000Z","provider":"openai","modelId":"gpt-4o"}
```

### ThinkingLevelChangeEntry

Emitted when the user changes the thinking/reasoning level.

```json
{"type":"thinking_level_change","id":"e5f6g7h8","parentId":"d4e5f6g7","timestamp":"2024-12-03T14:06:00.000Z","thinkingLevel":"high"}
```

### UsageEntry

Records model-attributed usage that is not an assistant message and does not participate in LLM context. `kind` is an arbitrary string identifying the operation; for example, cache warming uses `"cache_warm"`.

```json
{"type":"usage","id":"f6g7h8i9","parentId":"e5f6g7h8","timestamp":"2024-12-03T14:08:00.000Z","kind":"cache_warm","provider":"anthropic","model":"claude-sonnet-4-5","usage":{"input":0,"output":0,"cacheRead":50000,"cacheWrite":0,"totalTokens":50000,"cost":{"input":0,"output":0,"cacheRead":0.015,"cacheWrite":0,"total":0.015}}}
```

Usage entries contribute to session token and cost totals. Pi hides them from the conversation tree. Consumers should treat unknown `kind` values as normal usage rather than rejecting them.

### CompactionEntry

Created when context is compacted. Stores a summary of earlier messages and a complete system prompt/tool checkpoint.

```json
{"type":"compaction","id":"f6g7h8i9","parentId":"e5f6g7h8","timestamp":"2024-12-03T14:10:00.000Z","summary":"User discussed X, Y, Z...","firstKeptEntryId":"c3d4e5f6","tokensBefore":50000,"systemMessage":{"role":"system","content":"You are a coding assistant.","toolsAdded":[],"timestamp":1733235000000}}
```

`firstKeptEntryId` is required. It identifies the first entry retained from before the compaction entry. When rebuilding context, Pi replaces older summarized entries with the compaction summary and keeps the range beginning at this entry. A retain-none compaction stores its own ID in this field, so no preceding entries are retained.

Optional fields:
- `systemMessage`: The replayed prompt sections and tool declarations at the compaction boundary; it becomes the leading system message of the compacted context, and system messages among the kept entries are dropped in its favor. It is absent on older session entries.
- `usage`: LLM usage from generating the summary; included in session token and cost totals
- `details`: Implementation-specific data (e.g., `{ readFiles: string[], modifiedFiles: string[] }` for default, or custom data for extensions)
- `fromHook`: `true` if generated by an extension, `false`/`undefined` if pi-generated (legacy field name)

### ContextEditEntry

Append-only edit of one earlier context-producing entry. It changes only future model context; the target entry and its metadata remain unchanged in raw history, UI, exports, and session accounting.

```json
{"type":"context_edit","id":"g6h7i8j9","parentId":"f6g7h8i9","timestamp":"2024-12-03T14:11:00.000Z","targetId":"c3d4e5f6","replacement":null}
```

Targets may be user, assistant, tool-result, or custom-message entries. `replacement: null` omits the target from model context. A non-null `replacement` replaces only the target message content. String replacements for assistant and tool-result entries are normalized to one text block because those roles require content arrays. If several edits target the same entry, the latest edit on the active branch wins. Edits are branch-relative: navigating to a point before the edit reveals the target's original contribution again.

### BranchSummaryEntry

Created when switching branches via `/tree` with an LLM generated summary of the left branch up to the common ancestor. Captures context from the abandoned path.

```json
{"type":"branch_summary","id":"g7h8i9j0","parentId":"a1b2c3d4","timestamp":"2024-12-03T14:15:00.000Z","fromId":"f6g7h8i9","summary":"Branch explored approach A..."}
```

`parentId` is the entry from which the new branch continues. `fromId` is the previous leaf whose abandoned path was summarized.

Optional fields:
- `usage`: LLM usage from generating the summary; included in session token and cost totals
- `details`: File tracking data (`{ readFiles: string[], modifiedFiles: string[] }`) for default, or custom data for extensions
- `fromHook`: `true` if generated by an extension, `false`/`undefined` if pi-generated (legacy field name)

### CustomEntry

Extension state persistence. Does NOT participate in LLM context.

```json
{"type":"custom","id":"h8i9j0k1","parentId":"g7h8i9j0","timestamp":"2024-12-03T14:20:00.000Z","customType":"my-extension","data":{"count":42}}
```

Use `customType` to identify your extension's entries on reload. Interactive mode can render custom entries via `pi.registerEntryRenderer(customType, renderer)`, but they still do not participate in LLM context.

Pi stores [virtual model](virtual-models.md) router state as custom entries with `customType` `pi.virtual-model-state` and `data` `{ provider, modelId, state }`.

### CustomMessageEntry

Extension-injected messages that DO participate in LLM context.

```json
{"type":"custom_message","id":"i9j0k1l2","parentId":"h8i9j0k1","timestamp":"2024-12-03T14:25:00.000Z","customType":"my-extension","content":"Injected context...","display":true}
```

Fields:
- `content`: String or `(TextContent | ImageContent)[]` (same as UserMessage)
- `display`: `true` = show in TUI with distinct styling, `false` = hidden
- `details`: Optional extension-specific metadata (not sent to LLM)

### LabelEntry

User-defined bookmark/marker on an entry.

```json
{"type":"label","id":"j0k1l2m3","parentId":"i9j0k1l2","timestamp":"2024-12-03T14:30:00.000Z","targetId":"a1b2c3d4","label":"checkpoint-1"}
```

Set `label` to `undefined` to clear a label.

### SessionInfoEntry

Session metadata (e.g., user-defined display name). Set via `/name`, `--name` / `-n`, or `pi.setSessionName()` in extensions.

```json
{"type":"session_info","id":"k1l2m3n4","parentId":"j0k1l2m3","timestamp":"2024-12-03T14:35:00.000Z","name":"Refactor auth module"}
```

The session name is displayed in the session selector (`/resume`) instead of the first message when set.

## Tree Structure

Entries normally form one tree, but navigation APIs can create multiple roots:
- A root entry has `parentId: null`; the first entry is initially the root
- Each non-root entry points to its parent via `parentId`
- Branching creates new children from an earlier entry
- The "leaf" is the current position in the tree
- Calling `resetLeaf()` or `branchWithSummary(null, ...)` allows a later entry to become another root

```
[user msg] ─── [assistant] ─── [user msg] ─── [assistant] ─┬─ [user msg] ← current leaf
                                                            │
                                                            └─ [branch_summary] ─── [user msg] ← alternate branch
```

## Context Building

`buildContextEntries()` walks from the current leaf to the root, producing the active entry list while honoring compaction:

1. Collects all entries on the path
2. If one or more `CompactionEntry` values are on the path, uses the latest one:
   - Includes the compaction entry first
   - Includes non-system entries from `firstKeptEntryId` up to, but not including, the compaction entry
   - Includes entries after the compaction entry
3. Preserves non-message entries in the selected range so interactive mode can render them

`buildSessionProjection()` then applies the latest `context_edit` for each selected target. It returns the model-visible messages together with their source entries. Omitted targets produce no message; replacements retain the source entry's role and metadata while changing only content. The raw selected entries are not modified.

`buildSessionContext()` builds on that projection to produce the message list for the LLM:

1. Extracts current model and thinking level settings from the full path
2. Converts selected entries to messages:
   - `message` -> stored `AgentMessage`
   - `compaction` -> complete system checkpoint followed by `compactionSummary`
   - `branch_summary` -> `branchSummary`
   - `custom_message` -> `CustomMessage`
   - `context_edit` -> no context message of its own
   - `usage` and `custom` -> no context message

The compaction summary replaces entries before `firstKeptEntryId`. Pre-compaction system messages are folded into the complete checkpoint rather than replayed from the retained range. Retained non-system entries and all entries after the compaction remain available to the LLM.

## Parsing Example

```typescript
import { readFileSync } from "fs";

const lines = readFileSync("session.jsonl", "utf8").trim().split("\n");

for (const line of lines) {
  const entry = JSON.parse(line);

  switch (entry.type) {
    case "session":
      console.log(`Session v${entry.version ?? 1}: ${entry.id}`);
      break;
    case "message":
      console.log(`[${entry.id}] ${entry.message.role}: ${JSON.stringify(entry.message.content)}`);
      break;
    case "compaction":
      console.log(`[${entry.id}] Compaction: ${entry.tokensBefore} tokens summarized`);
      break;
    case "branch_summary":
      console.log(`[${entry.id}] Branch from ${entry.fromId}`);
      break;
    case "usage":
      console.log(`[${entry.id}] Usage (${entry.kind}): ${entry.usage.totalTokens} tokens`);
      break;
    case "custom":
      console.log(`[${entry.id}] Custom (${entry.customType}): ${JSON.stringify(entry.data)}`);
      break;
    case "custom_message":
      console.log(`[${entry.id}] Extension message (${entry.customType}): ${entry.content}`);
      break;
    case "label":
      console.log(`[${entry.id}] Label "${entry.label}" on ${entry.targetId}`);
      break;
    case "model_change":
      console.log(`[${entry.id}] Model: ${entry.provider}/${entry.modelId}`);
      break;
    case "thinking_level_change":
      console.log(`[${entry.id}] Thinking: ${entry.thinkingLevel}`);
      break;
  }
}
```

# Sessions and Context

Pi saves a conversation as a session. The active branch of that session supplies conversation history for the next model request. Use session commands to continue work, explore another branch, or reduce the amount of history sent to the model.

## Continue or switch sessions

Pi saves sessions automatically unless you start it with `--no-session`.

```bash
pi --continue
pi --resume
```

`--continue` opens the most recent session for the current directory. `--resume` opens the session picker. In interactive mode, `/resume` opens the same picker and `/new` starts a new session.

Each session records the working directory it was created in and never changes it. Pi runs a session in its working directory, so tools, `@path` references, project configuration, and context files resolve from there.

| Entry point | Working directory |
|---|---|
| `--continue` | The current directory |
| `--resume`, `/resume`, `--session`, `/import` | The session's working directory, which can differ from the current directory |
| `--fork`, or a `--session` ID from another directory that you choose to fork | The current directory, in a new session |

If a session's working directory no longer exists, for example after the project folder was renamed, interactive mode asks how to open it:

- **Continue** runs the session in the current directory. Pi does not store that choice, so it asks again the next time you open the session.
- **Fork** copies the session into the current directory as a new session with a new ID, like `--fork`. The original stays unchanged. At startup the copy is stored like other new sessions for the current directory; from `/resume` or `/import` it is stored next to the current session, like `/new`.
- **Cancel** leaves the current session open, or exits at startup.

Other modes exit with an error.

Use `/name` or `--name` to assign a recognizable session name. Run `/session` to verify the current session file, ID, message count, token usage, and cost.

The session picker lets you search, rename, and delete sessions. It can also show paths, change sorting, and limit results to named sessions. See [Keybindings](keybindings.md#sessions) for its shortcuts.

## Choose how to branch

Pi stores entries as a tree, so returning to an earlier point does not erase the branch you leave.

| Action | Result | Use it when |
|---|---|---|
| `/tree` | Moves within the current session file | Related alternatives should stay together |
| `/fork` | Creates a new session from an earlier user message | The alternative should become separate work |
| `/clone` | Copies the active branch into a new session | You want a separate copy of the current state |

In `/tree`, select a user message to put its text back in the editor. Edit and submit it to create another branch. Selecting an assistant response or another entry continues after that entry with an empty editor.

When you leave a branch, Pi can summarize it and attach that summary to the branch you enter. This preserves relevant work from the abandoned path without including every message from it.

For the persisted tree and entry types, see [Session Format](session-format.md).

## Manage conversation context

The model receives the active branch, not every branch in the session file. Pi combines that history with the system prompt, discovered context files, available tools, and loaded skill descriptions. [How Pi Works](how-pi-works.md#context) describes how those inputs are assembled.

The footer shows current context usage. When the active context approaches the model's limit, Pi normally compacts older history automatically. Compaction adds a summary and keeps recent messages. It does not delete the original session entries.

Run `/compact` to compact manually. You can add instructions when the summary should preserve a particular topic or decision. Configure automatic compaction and retained history through [Settings](settings.md#compaction).

Compaction can fail if the provider is unavailable or cannot accept the summarization request. Correct the provider problem and run `/compact` again. Disabling automatic compaction does not disable the manual command.

See [Compaction Reference](compaction.md) for thresholds, retained boundaries, branch-summary behavior, and extension hooks.

## Control session storage

By default, Pi stores sessions under `~/.pi/agent/sessions/`, grouped by working directory. Use `--session-dir`, `PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR`, or the `sessionDir` setting to choose another location. The CLI option has highest precedence.

Use `--no-session` for an ephemeral run. An ephemeral session cannot be resumed after Pi exits.

## Export or share a session

Use `/export` to write the current session as HTML or JSONL. Use `/share` to upload it and get a viewer link. By default, Pi uses a Radius artifact when Radius authentication is configured; otherwise, it uses a private GitHub gist. Set [`sessionShareDestination`](settings.md#sessions-and-context) to `gist` or `radius` to force one destination.

Review exported or shared sessions first. They can contain prompts, model responses, tool arguments, command output, file contents, and extension messages.

## Report a bug

Run `/bug [description]` to prepare a private report for the Pi developers. You can include the session transcript, omit it, or ask the current model to summarize the problem. Review any transcript or generated summary because it can contain sensitive conversation data.

The report includes environment and provider configuration without credential values, plus recorded error diagnostics. Upload it through `radius.pi.dev` or export the same report as a zip to inspect and share yourself. Uploads do not require a login; Radius authentication attributes the report to your account so the developers can follow up. If an upload fails, Pi offers to export the zip.

- **Steers** are placed after the current tool round and join the running work.
- **Follow-ups** are placed when the run answers, and start the next run.
- **`whenIdle: "reject"`** refuses an input when no run is working, so it never starts a run of its own. With `whenBusy: "steer"`, it steers the current run or throws `ConversationIdle`. A run that answered and waits for its [after-run tasks](#work-at-the-end-of-a-run) is still working, so such an input queues and starts the next run.
- **`admit(tx, draft)`** admits inside your own commit, with the same rules, and returns the submission's ID. Your checks, the admission, and your writes are stored together or not at all:

  ```typescript
  const id = await harness.commit(async (tx) => {
    const chat = await tx.doc(MyChat, root.id); // your own conversation document
    if (chat.muted.includes(userId)) throw new Error("Muted");
    const id = await root.admit(tx, { type: "input", content: text, whenBusy: "steer", whenIdle: "reject" });
    chat.sent.push({ id, userId }); // your own state, same commit
    return id;
  }, context);
  ```

  Call it before the commit's own table writes (`appendEntry()`, `createTask()`, another admission), once per commit: otherwise it throws `ReadAfterWrite`, on every path. Documents may be read and written before and after it. A rejection (`ConversationBusy`, `ConversationIdle`) throws before any write, so you may catch it. Until your commit is stored the admission is provisional: if your callback throws later, no submission exists. Tasks and tools do the same in their own commits through `api.conversation(id)`; entries the admission places carry the task's `byTaskId`.
- **Writes** append an entry without asking the model anything. A write of only `kind` and `data` changes nothing the model sees, so it is appended at once, even mid-run, and is never queued: a chat message shows in the transcript as soon as it is sent. It can therefore appear before items submitted earlier that are still queued, except behind a queued reset, where it waits so the reset does not hide it. A write with `model`, `head`, or `edits` waits for the next boundary like a steer.
- `await submission.abort(context)` withdraws a queued submission.

## Concepts

- **Harness**: one open storage plus the machinery that runs agents on it. All changes go through one line of atomic commits, and nothing is shown before its commit is stored.
- **Conversation**: a transcript. `root()` creates the root conversation on first use; you can create more and fork them. A `Conversation` handle holds no state; compare handles by `id`.
- **Entry**: one immutable transcript record, such as a user message (`pi.user`), a model response (`pi.assistant`), a tool result (`pi.tool-result`), a system prompt change (`pi.system`), a reset (`pi.reset`), or your own kind. The model sees the entries from the newest reset onward.
- **Commit**: an atomic write. `conversation.commit((tx) => ...)` can append entries, edit documents, and create tasks together; either all of it is stored or none of it.
- **Document**: typed JSON state stored next to the transcript and changed in commits. Built-in ones hold each conversation's agent choices (`pi.agent`), provider-facing session identity (`pi.provider`), running generation and tools (`pi.live`), queued submissions (`pi.inbox`), and spend (`pi.usage`).
- **Task**: a durable state machine that saves a checkpoint at every step, so a restarted process continues from the last one. Every task has an owner: its conversation, or another task. The Harness runs answers as built-in tasks: `pi.generation` calls the model and owns the `pi.tool` tasks of its tool calls, waits for them, and hands the run to the next generation.
- **Submission**: something you hand to a conversation, either user input or an entry to write, which you can wait for.
- **Turn and run**: a turn is one model response and its tool calls; a run is the turns from an input to its final answer. A conversation is busy while a run is going.
- **Extension**: a named bundle of tools, system prompt sections, hooks, wrappers, and tasks.
- **Registry**: the extensions this process installed. It can change while the Harness runs; new work uses the new state.
- **Agent**: what a conversation runs with: model, thinking level, selected extensions, tools, instructions, and working directory. Stored per conversation as names in `pi.agent`, resolved against the registry at each use.

One answered input, as entries and tasks:

```text
submit(input) → pi.user
  pi.generation → pi.system (only if the prompt or tools changed), pi.assistant (tool calls)
    pi.tool × n → pi.tool-result × n   (owned by the generation, which waits for them)
  pi.generation → pi.assistant (answer) → submission done
```

## Persist and Resume

Use SQLite or JSONL storage to keep conversations across restarts:

```typescript
import { openNodeSqliteStorage } from "@earendil-works/pi-durable/storage/sqlite/node";

const harness = await Harness.open(await openNodeSqliteStorage("./session.sqlite"), { models, registry }, context);
const root = await harness.root(context); // the same root as last time
harness.resume(); // continue any run the last process left unfinished
```

Work interrupted by a crash or close stays pending. `resume()` starts the task scheduler; submitting or waiting starts it too. A process that only shows a session another one drives opens it with `readOnly: true`: open recovers nothing, and every write, `resume()`, and every call that would run tasks rejects with `ReadOnlySession`. That option covers the Harness, not the storage open before it: open JSONL storage with `openNodeJsonlStorage(directory, context, { readOnly: true })` too, since a writable JSONL open repairs files the writer may be appending to (see [Storage](#storage)). SQLite storage opens as usual: SQLite's file locks keep it safe beside the writer. Each conversation has its own persisted UUIDv7 in `pi.provider`, forwarded to pi-ai as `sessionId` for provider prompt-cache and session affinity. It survives reopen, retries, reset, compaction, and model changes; a child or fork receives a fresh identity. A legacy conversation receives and persists one before its first generation or compaction request.

A retried submission with the same `requestId` returns the existing submission instead of submitting twice:

```typescript
const submission = await root.submit({ type: "input", content: "Hello", requestId: "greeting-1" }, context);
// After a restart: the same request ID finds the same submission.
const again = await root.submit({ type: "input", content: "Hello", requestId: "greeting-1" }, context);
// again.id === submission.id
```

`harness.submission(id)` reacquires a submission by ID, for example to wait for it after a restart.

### Sleeping and Waking Up

### Failures and Recovery

**Crash loops.** Work that deterministically crashes its process, by exhausting memory or CPU before its next checkpoint, would otherwise be resumed and crash again forever. A model request the host died during is a failed attempt under `settings.retry`: its partial answer is kept as an aborted entry, the next attempt waits for the backoff (shown in `docs["pi.live"].generation.retry`), and with no retry left the run ends with `docs["pi.live"].runFailure` reason `interrupted`. A deferred response that was being fetched is polled again as the next attempt, not requested again, and cancelled when the run ends. A close is not a crash: a request it stopped is sent again. Other work is counted: open counts each task a crash, eviction, or reset cut off, and a new state the task commits starts the count over. Once the count reaches `settings.restartLimit` (default 5; `Infinity` never ends a task for it), the task ends instead of running again: a tool call with an error result (diagnostic code `restart_limit`), a compaction failed into `compactionFailure`, a run with `runFailure` reason `restart_limit` (also when charging an interrupted request keeps crashing), and a task of your own kinds `faulted`, reported as `task_faulted` with reason `restart_limit`. The built-in ones are reported as `task_interrupted`, as is a run that ends `interrupted`, so a crash loop always reaches `onReport`. Every task running when a process dies is counted, not only the one that killed it. An abort handler cut off that many times ends its task `faulted` too; a run someone aborted still ends `aborted`, with the cut-off in `detail`.

**Reports.** `onReport(report)` gets one `Report`: the `error` and what happened in `report.kind`: `storage_failed` for the error that failed the Harness (a Storage error, often a platform reset); `task_faulted`, `task_interrupted` (crashes ended it, with `report.reason` and `report.restarts`), `migration_failed`, `task_outdated` (`reason` `missing_task`, `task_too_old`, or `migration_failed`, the words a blocked task shows), or `task_error` for a task, with `report.task` (its `id`, `kind`, and `conversationId`) and the extension that installed it in `report.extension`; `extension_error` for hooks, sections, wrappers, and tools, with the extension's name; `host_error` for a host callback, named in `report.callback`; and `listener_error`. A host can feed `task_faulted` reports of one kind to its own breaker.

**Queued inputs after a failed run.** A run that fails with a model error, a missing model, nothing to answer, its turn limit, or crashes (`interrupted`, `restart_limit`) leaves the inputs queued behind it waiting until the next input arrives. `settings.afterFailedRun` changes that: `continue` starts the next run with them, as after an answer, and `withdraw` settles them `unanswered` with reason `run_failed`.

**Blocked tasks.** Tasks blocked on a missing or unmigratable definition show their reason in the task graph too, and a registry change that unblocks them makes `onWake` report the Session active, so a host need not poll them.

### Failures and Recovery

**Crash loops.** Work that deterministically crashes its process, by exhausting memory or CPU before its next checkpoint, would otherwise be resumed and crash again forever. A model request the host died during is a failed attempt under `settings.retry`: its partial answer is kept as an aborted entry, the next attempt waits for the backoff (shown in `docs["pi.live"].generation.retry`), and with no retry left the run ends with `docs["pi.live"].runFailure` reason `interrupted`. A deferred response that was being fetched is polled again as the next attempt, not requested again, and cancelled when the run ends. A close is not a crash: a request it stopped is sent again. Other work is counted: open counts each task a crash, eviction, or reset cut off, and a new state the task commits starts the count over. Once the count reaches `settings.restartLimit` (default 5; `Infinity` never ends a task for it), the task ends instead of running again: a tool call with an error result (diagnostic code `restart_limit`), a compaction failed into `compactionFailure`, a run with `runFailure` reason `restart_limit` (also when charging an interrupted request keeps crashing), and a task of your own kinds `faulted`, reported as `task_faulted` with reason `restart_limit`. The built-in ones are reported as `task_interrupted`, as is a run that ends `interrupted`, so a crash loop always reaches `onReport`. Every task running when a process dies is counted, not only the one that killed it. An abort handler cut off that many times ends its task `faulted` too; a run someone aborted still ends `aborted`, with the cut-off in `detail`.

**Reports.** `onReport(report)` gets one `Report`: the `error` and what happened in `report.kind`: `storage_failed` for the error that failed the Harness (a Storage error, often a platform reset); `task_faulted`, `task_interrupted` (crashes ended it, with `report.reason` and `report.restarts`), `migration_failed`, `task_outdated` (`reason` `missing_task`, `task_too_old`, or `migration_failed`, the words a blocked task shows), or `task_error` for a task, with `report.task` (its `id`, `kind`, and `conversationId`) and the extension that installed it in `report.extension`; `extension_error` for hooks, sections, wrappers, and tools, with the extension's name; `host_error` for a host callback, named in `report.callback`; and `listener_error`. A host can feed `task_faulted` reports of one kind to its own breaker.

**Queued inputs after a failed run.** A run that fails with a model error, a missing model, nothing to answer, its turn limit, or crashes (`interrupted`, `restart_limit`) leaves the inputs queued behind it waiting until the next input arrives. `settings.afterFailedRun` changes that: `continue` starts the next run with them, as after an answer, and `withdraw` settles them `unanswered` with reason `run_failed`.

**Blocked tasks.** Tasks blocked on a missing or unmigratable definition show their reason in the task graph too, and a registry change that unblocks them makes `onWake` report the Session active, so a host need not poll them.

## Concepts

- **Harness**: one open storage plus the machinery that runs agents on it. All changes go through one line of atomic commits, and nothing is shown before its commit is stored.
- **Conversation**: a transcript. `root()` creates the root conversation on first use; you can create more and fork them. A `Conversation` handle holds no state; compare handles by `id`.
- **Entry**: one immutable transcript record, such as a user message (`pi.user`), a model response (`pi.assistant`), a tool result (`pi.tool-result`), a system prompt change (`pi.system`), a reset (`pi.reset`), or your own kind. The model sees the entries from the newest reset onward.
- **Commit**: an atomic write. `conversation.commit((tx) => ...)` can append entries, edit documents, and create tasks together; either all of it is stored or none of it.
- **Document**: typed JSON state stored next to the transcript and changed in commits. Built-in ones hold each conversation's agent choices (`pi.agent`), provider-facing session identity (`pi.provider`), running generation and tools (`pi.live`), queued submissions (`pi.inbox`), and spend (`pi.usage`).
- **Task**: a durable state machine that saves a checkpoint at every step, so a restarted process continues from the last one. Every task has an owner: its conversation, or another task. The Harness runs answers as built-in tasks: `pi.generation` calls the model and owns the `pi.tool` tasks of its tool calls, waits for them, and hands the run to the next generation.
- **Submission**: something you hand to a conversation, either user input or an entry to write, which you can wait for.
- **Turn and run**: a turn is one model response and its tool calls; a run is the turns from an input to its final answer. A conversation is busy while a run is going.
- **Extension**: a named bundle of tools, system prompt sections, hooks, wrappers, and tasks.
- **Registry**: the extensions this process installed. It can change while the Harness runs; new work uses the new state.
- **Agent**: what a conversation runs with: model, thinking level, selected extensions, tools, instructions, and working directory. Stored per conversation as names in `pi.agent`, resolved against the registry at each use.

One answered input, as entries and tasks:

```text
submit(input) → pi.user
  pi.generation → pi.system (only if the prompt or tools changed), pi.assistant (tool calls)
    pi.tool × n → pi.tool-result × n   (owned by the generation, which waits for them)
  pi.generation → pi.assistant (answer) → submission done
```

Sources: spec = `packages/durable/docs/spec.md`, README = `packages/durable/README.md`, both on `main` of https://github.com/earendil-works/pi. I read them as raw files and did not run any trial. Spec line numbers refer to the file as of 2026-11-23.

## 1. Lifecycle of a model request task and a tool call task

**Model request: `pi.generation`** (spec §8.3, https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/packages/durable/docs/spec.md; version 3)

The checkpoint phases are `prepare` (initial, `{phase:"prepare", attempt:1}`), `request`, `retry`, `poll`, `tools`, `finish`, `drain`, `afterTools` and `yield`.

- **`prepare`**
  - One commit appends the planned `pi.system` entries and moves to `request`.
  - The checkpoint then holds model, thinkingLevel, streamOptions and `cutoff` (the newest entry included in the request).
  - Resume: it runs again from the top.
- **`request`**
  - Before the call, `pi.live.generation` is set (attempt number) by a deferred commit.
  - Partial output is committed as `pi.live.generation.message`, throttled to every 100 ms by default. These commits are deferred: watches see them at once, and storage gets them with the next commit that reads `pi.live`, or within `persistWithinMs` (default 1000 ms).
  - The terminal message is classified in one commit that also clears the partial.
    - `stop`/`length` appends the `pi.assistant` entry.
    - `toolUse` appends the assistant entry and starts the tool round, moving to `tools`.
    - A retryable `error` appends the error entry and sleeps at `retry`.
    - A deferred response sleeps at `poll`.
    - Any other error, or `aborted` without an abort mark, appends the error entry and fails the task.
  - Resume after a close: the request is re-sent with the same committed messages, model, thinking level and stream options, and `beforeRequest` runs again.
  - Resume after a crash (the record's `restarts` > 0):
    - A leftover stored partial is first converted into an `aborted` `pi.assistant` entry.
    - The attempt counts as failed. If the retry policy allows it, the task sleeps at `retry`, with the note "The host stopped while the model was answering, on attempt N".
    - Otherwise the run ends `interrupted`.
    - It is not re-sent immediately. After `restartLimit` crashes the run ends `restart_limit`.
  - A crash before the first store leaves no aborted entry, and that attempt's usage is not recorded.
- **`retry`**: waits until `until`, then returns to `prepare` with the next attempt. If run before `until`, it sleeps again.
- **`poll`**
  - The checkpoint holds the deferred `handle` and `pollAt`.
  - On resume after a crash, a fetch that was in flight is charged as a failed attempt, but the deferred response is polled again instead of re-requesting.
- **`tools`**: the task waits (`waiting` status, `allSettled`) on the round's tool tasks.
- **`finish`, `drain`, `afterTools`, `yield`**: these are about hooks that run after a round or after the answer (afterRun, afterTools and onYield tasks). The abort and restart-limit rules for these phases are in spec §8.3.

**Tool call: `pi.tool`** (spec §8.4; version 4)

The checkpoint phases are `call` (initial), `execute` and `parked`. The spec comments `execute` as "Intent: `execute()` runs in the phase that commits it; reached as a phase only by recovery."

- **`call`**
  - It validates the arguments and runs the `beforeTool` chain.
  - A deferred commit sets the slot in `pi.live.tools` to `running`.
  - One commit then records intent: it moves to `execute` with the final arguments and `replay: "safe" | "unsafe"`.
  - `execute()` runs in the same handler, then `afterTool` runs.
  - The result commit appends one `pi.tool-result` entry, marks the slot `done` and completes with `{entryId, control}`.
  - A tool that does not resolve, invalid arguments, or a block commit an error result with no intent.
- **Partial output**
  - Running output lives in the slot (`output`, `details`, `diagnostics`) as throttled, deferred commits (default 100 ms).
  - Each run of `execute()` starts with empty output.
- **`execute`** (reached only by recovery)
  - If the stored and the current policy are both `safe`, it executes again with the stored arguments, wake and checkpoint, without `beforeTool`.
  - Otherwise it commits an `interrupted` error result built from the durable partial output, and the task ends `failed`. If the run had been woken from a park, `cancel` runs first. The README says the same: "reruns on reopen only when it is declared `replay: "safe"`; otherwise the model gets an `interrupted` error result with the output committed so far."
  - A close and a crash both leave `execute`, so a replay-unsafe run is never repeated.
  - After `restartLimit` cut-offs it commits a `restart_limit` error result instead.
- **`parked`**
  - A tool can return a park (`sleeping` or `waiting`). One commit stores the latest details and diagnostics and the `parked` checkpoint.
  - The `parked` handler runs when the park is woken. It commits intent (`execute` with the wake and checkpoint) and runs `execute()` again.
  - A restart while parked runs no tool code (README line 426).
- **Abort**: for `parked`, or `execute` with a wake, `cancel` runs first. An `aborted` error result is then committed from the slot's durable partial output.

**Shared pattern:** spec §5.2 "Effect sandwich" is "commit intent phase / perform external effect / commit outcome or next phase". Its rule is that "Reopening in an intent phase means the effect may have happened."

The word "safe" is a tool's `replay` field. "Interrupted notice" is the result the model gets in the transcript.

## 2. Commit, entries, tasks, documents

Spec §1 states the core rule: "A Session atomically commits immutable entries, full task records, and Chord-tracked documents. Only committed state is observable."

- An entry (`EntryRecord`) is an immutable transcript record in one conversation. Its fields are `id`, `conversationId`, `kind`, optional `model` (messages), `data`, `head`, `edits` and `byTaskId`. Entry ids are Session-global, ordered and never reused.
- A task is a durable state machine, stored as a `TaskRecord` holding its input, a checkpoint and a state (`pending`, `running`, `waiting`, `sleeping`, `completing`, `terminal`).
- Memos are small JSON values inside the live task record.
- A document is mutable JSON, stored as one base plus later deltas (Chord ops).
- The storage layer (§10) takes a commit as a batch of writes: `conversation`, `entry`, `task`, `submission`, `document.create`, `document.copy`, `document.change` and `document.retire`. All are atomic with one `seq`. The mutation line runs one commit callback at a time, and storage writes are group-committed.
- Deferred commits may touch only existing conversation documents. They are visible to watchers before they are stored, and a crash loses them.
- A terminal task transition writes the terminal record, appends result entries, retires the task's documents and settles submissions in one commit (§5.3).

## 3. defineTask, sleepUntil, signals

- **`defineTask`** (§5.1): the definition is `{name, version, initial(input), phases, abort, migrate?, hooks?}`. `phases` is a handler per `phase` value in the checkpoint. A phase handler ends by calling `runtime.commit(...)` with the next state: `running` with a new checkpoint, `waiting`, `sleeping` or `terminal`. After a crash or close, a phase reruns from its top. `abort` is the handler for aborts.
- **`runtime.sleepUntil(until, checkpoint, context)`** (§5.6): it commits a sleep and resolves when the sleep is stored. The phase then returns, and the task resumes at the checkpoint once the Harness clock (`HarnessOptions.now`, epoch ms) reaches `until`. Deadlines survive reopens. The spec says "There is no sleep inside a phase", so work after the wait goes in the next phase. Work before the sleep is not exactly-once.
- **Signals** (§5.7): `defineSignal({name, version, schema})` gives a token, and `token.key("k")` names one wait.
  - A task sleeps with `{status:"sleeping", signals:[...], until?}`.
  - `harness.signal()` or `tx.signal()` delivers a value, with result `delivered`, `duplicate`, `invalid`, `closed` or `not_found`.
  - The value is stored in the task's memos as `pi.signal.<name>/<key>`. A value delivered early is kept.
  - On wake, `runtime.readSignal` returns `{kind:"value"}` or `{kind:"expired"}`.
  - The wake reason is `time`, `expired`, `signal` or `tasks`. Each key can wake a task only once.

## 4. Pi coding agent sessions

Sources: `session-format.md` and `sessions.md` under https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/tree/main/packages/coding-agent/docs. I also read `src/core/session-manager.ts`.

- **Storage:** JSONL at `~/.pi/agent/sessions/--<path>--/<timestamp>_<session-id>.jsonl`. The header is currently version 3.
- **Entry types:** `session` (header, not in the tree), `message`, `model_change`, `thinking_level_change`, `usage`, `compaction`, `context_edit`, `branch_summary`, `custom`, `custom_message`, `label` and `session_info`.
- **Tree:** every non-header entry has `id`, `parentId` (null for a root) and an ISO `timestamp`. Branching adds children to an earlier entry, in the same file. The leaf is the current position.
- **Context building:** it walks leaf to root and honours the latest compaction (`firstKeptEntryId`).
- **When entries are appended** (source code only): `_appendEntry` calls `_persist`, which does a synchronous `appendFileSync` of one line per entry. The file is created lazily on the first persist after the session contains a user or assistant message. At that point all entries so far are written in one go.
- **In-flight turn if the process dies:** neither doc says anything about this. I found no statement in `session-format.md`, `sessions.md`, `sdk.md` or `how-pi-works.md`. From the code, an entry is only in the file once `_appendEntry` ran for it. I did not verify at which agent event (for example, message end) the manager appends. The docs and code I read show no resume or repair of a partial turn.

## 5. ExecutionEnv

- **Interface:** `ExecutionEnv extends FileSystem, Shell` (`packages/durable/src/env/index.ts`, `@earendil-works/pi-durable/env`).
  - `FileSystem` has `id`, `absolutePath`, `joinPath`, `readTextFile`, `openTextLineReader`, `readTextLines`, `readBinaryFile`, `openBinaryReader`, `writeFile`, `appendFile`, `truncateFile`, `flushFile`, `renameFile`, `fileInfo`, `listDir`, optional `listFiles`, `openDirReader`, `watch`, `canonicalPath`, `exists`, `createDir`, `remove`, `createTempDir`, `createTempFile` and `cleanup`.
  - `Shell` has `exec(command: string | string[], options, context)` and `cleanup`. A string command runs through a shell; an array runs the program directly.
  - Methods return `Result<T, FileError | ExecutionError>`.
- **`NodeExecutionEnv`:** import from `@earendil-works/pi-durable/env/node`, constructed as `new NodeExecutionEnv({cwd})`. It does not implement `listFiles`.
- **pi-env** (https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/tree/main/packages/env):
  - `RemoteExecutionEnv({connection, id, cwd})` talks to a Rust daemon over SSH. It implements `listFiles`.
  - `LocalExecutionEnv({cwd, connection})` is `NodeExecutionEnv` plus `listFiles` through a local daemon.
- **Can the env change between tool calls?** Yes, per the README and spec, both documentation:
  - `HarnessOptions.env(target)` receives `{conversationId, cwd, read}`. README: "builds the execution environment for each tool call".
  - A tool's `api.env` is built right before executing (§8.4). A fresh object per call is fine.
  - `edit` and `write` serialize per env `id` and path, so equal ids must mean the same files.
  - A throw from `env` becomes the call's error result.
  - Because the function runs per call and receives `read`, an app can return a different env (different `cwd` or container) on a later call. The docs say "one container per conversation" is the intended use but do not describe switching mid-conversation. I did not run a trial.

## 6. watch and submit

- **`conversation.watch(context, window?)`** (README §Watching a Conversation, spec §9.3) returns a watch.
  - `watch.value` is the view at attachment. `watch.start(listener)` receives `{kind:"value", value, ops, retired}` calls.
  - `stop()` and `closed` give a `WatchEnd`: `stopped`, `aborted`, `ended`, `listener_error` or `failed`.
  - The window is `{from?, min=50, max=2*min}`.
  - Related methods:
    - `harness.observeConversation`, `observeTaskGraph` and `observeDoc`: synchronous observers with `advance` and `detach`.
    - `ConversationTranscript` helpers: `merge`, `loadEarlier`, `fillGap`, `resume`.
    - `conversation.entries()`: paged scans.
- **`watchEvents()`:** I found no such name in the README, the spec, `packages/coding-agent/docs/sdk.md` or `packages/durable/src/env`. I did not search the rest of the repository.
- **`submit(draft, context)`:**
  - `type:"input"` takes `content`, `whenBusy?: "steer" | "followUp" | "reject"`, `whenIdle?: "reject"`, `onAbort?: "withdraw" | "keep"`, `requestId?` and `notify?`.
  - `type:"write"` takes `entry`. `type:"continue"` takes nothing.
  - The default `whenBusy` is follow-up.
  - `"reject"` throws `ConversationBusy`; `whenIdle:"reject"` throws `ConversationIdle`.
  - Steers are placed after the current tool round. Follow-ups are placed when the run answers and start the next run.
  - Related methods: `admit(tx, draft)` (the same admission inside your own commit), `submission.wait()`, `submission.abort(context)`, `harness.submission(id)`.
  - The same `requestId` returns the same submission.
- **What a late client receives:**
  - The README says "A client that joins late or reconnects starts from the current view; nothing is replayed."
  - That view is the newest 50 entries plus `pi.live`, `pi.inbox`, `pi.usage`, `pi.agent` and `pi.provider`, including the in-progress partial.
  - With `from`, it gets entries after that id. If more than 10,000 ops are pending, a client gets one root replacement `[["r", view]]`.

## Not verified

- No trial was run, so nothing above is a verified fact. All of it comes from source and documentation.
- Pi coding-agent behaviour when the process dies mid-turn, and the agent event at which entries are appended.
- `watchEvents()`: no source found.
- Whether an env can be switched mid-conversation: stated by inference from the per-call builder only.
- Package versions and release dates were not collected. The package files were not read and the question did not ask for them.
